description.en: Transfer of vehicle ownership (RC Transfer) is the legal process of changing the registered owner's name on a vehicle's Registration Certificate (RC) when a vehicle is sold or transferred. Under the Motor Vehicles Act, the transfer must be intimated to the RTO within 14 days of the sale. Both buyer and seller must file the necessary forms.

verifiedConditions.claim: The vehicle must be currently registered with an RTO in India with a valid or expired Registration Certificate.
The vehicle must not have any pending road tax, fines, or challans. All dues must be cleared before transfer.

unverifiedEligibility: If the vehicle is under hypothecation (loan), a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the financing bank/institution is required.
Vehicles involved in criminal cases or under court attachment cannot be transferred.
Inter-state transfer requires an NOC from the original registering RTO.
Transfer of a vehicle within 12 months of first registration may require payment of additional road tax in some states.

requirements.claim: Form 29 (Notice of Transfer of Ownership of a Motor Vehicle) signed by both the transferor (seller) and transferee (buyer), submitted to the RTO.
Form 30 (Report of Transfer of Ownership of a Motor Vehicle) signed by the transferee (buyer), reporting the transfer to the registering authority.
Original Registration Certificate (RC) of the vehicle.
Valid motor vehicle insurance certificate transferred to or obtained in the buyer's name.
Valid Pollution Under Control (PUC) certificate for the vehicle.
Identity and address proof of both the buyer and seller — Aadhaar card, voter ID, passport, or driving license.
If the vehicle is hypothecated (under a loan), a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the financing bank or institution is required to remove the hypothecation endorsement.

processInformation.claim: The seller fills Form 29 and the buyer fills Form 30, both with signatures. These forms can be submitted online through the Vahan portal or physically at the RTO within 14 days of the sale.

The buyer submits the completed forms along with all required documents (RC, insurance, PUC, identity proof, sale receipt or agreement, NOC from bank if applicable) to the RTO where the vehicle is registered.
Pay the transfer fee and applicable road tax (if any) at the RTO or online through the Vahan portal.
The RTO verifies the documents, checks for pending challans or hypothecation, and processes the transfer. The vehicle may be inspected at the RTO if required.
A new RC smart card is issued in the buyer's name, or the existing RC is endorsed with the new owner's details. The updated RC is dispatched to the buyer's address.

output.claim: An updated Registration Certificate (RC) in the buyer's name reflecting the change of ownership. The vehicle's registration number remains the same; only the owner details are updated in the Vahan database and on the RC smart card.

fees.applicability: Vehicle ownership transfer fee (excluding road tax)
fees.claim: Transfer fee ranges from Rs. 300 to Rs. 500 depending on the state. Additional road tax may be payable if the vehicle is being transferred to another state or if the original tax period has expired.

processingTime.applicability: RC transfer from application to issuance of updated RC
processingTime.claim: Vehicle ownership transfer typically takes 7 to 30 days from the date of application, depending on the RTO workload and whether all documents are in order. Inter-state transfers may take longer due to NOC requirements.

sources.title: Vahan — National Vehicle Registration Portal
sources.publisher: Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The Vahan portal provides online services for vehicle ownership transfer, including form submission, fee payment, and status tracking.
claimsSupported: Form 29 and Form 30 are required for ownership transfer.
Transfer fee ranges from Rs. 300 to Rs. 500.
Online processing through Vahan portal is available.
NOC from bank required for hypothecated vehicles.
sources.uncertainty: Fee structures and processing timelines vary significantly by state.

sources.title: Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 — Section 50 (Transfer of Ownership)
sources.publisher: Ministry of Law and Justice, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: Section 50 provides that the transfer of ownership must be reported to the registering authority within 14 days. Both transferor and transferee must report the transfer using the prescribed forms.
claimsSupported: Transfer must be reported within 14 days.
Both buyer and seller must file forms.
Penalty for late reporting of transfer.
sources.uncertainty: Enforcement of the 14-day deadline varies across RTOs.

limitations: Fee structures and road tax implications of transfer vary significantly by state.
The record does not cover transfer of vehicles due to death of owner (succession-based transfer) which has different requirements.
Inter-state transfer involves additional NOC and re-registration processes not fully modeled here.
The record does not cover transfer of government or diplomatic vehicles.
Some states have introduced online transfer without physical RTO visit for specific cases, which is not captured.

review.reviewReason: Core transfer process verified from Motor Vehicles Act and Parivahan portal. State-specific fee structures and road tax implications need verification.
nextReviewTrigger: Changes to Motor Vehicles Act transfer provisions.
